song.title: Ever Fallen In Love (With Someone You Shouldn't've_)

guitar.evidence: Pete Shelley famously played an unusual Japanese-made "Starway" guitar; Steve Diggle played Gibson SG-style guitars. Documented within punk circles but not mainstream-iconic.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown at low confidence.

tone.target: bright jangly punk crunch with tight pick attack
tone.profile: bright jangly punk crunch with tight pick attack
tone.summary: A punchy, jangly punk tone achieved using a Boost for attack, Green OD for classic Plexi crunch, UK 45 amp model, and a dry cabinet setup to emphasize upper mids and tightness.

rig.name: The Buzzcocks - Ever Fallen In Love (With Someone You Shouldn't've_) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up pick noise and hum inherent in punk strumming.
Enhance the pick attack and sustain for a punchy punk sound.
Provide the classic British Plexi/Marshall crunch and mid-forward grit.
No dedicated distortion needed; Green OD provides sufficient crunch.
Simulate the bright, punchy British tone of a classic punk era amp.
Provide a classic British cabinet sound that complements the UK 45 amp model.
Boost upper mids and treble for jangliness while tightening the low end.
No wah needed; keep the tone direct and punchy.
Avoid noticeable delay effects as per the 'drop delay' instruction.
Add minimal, natural room ambience without sounding 'big' or muddy.
blocks.gap: The instruction was to keep it dry, so the reverb is kept very low and subtle.

improvements.summary: Replace the default cabinet IR with a more open, jangly British 2x12 or 4x12 to enhance upper mids and maintain tightness.

proposals.reason: Enhance jangly punk brightness and upper mids, while maintaining tight low end.
